_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401875556.overall: Willem II are bottom of the Eredivisie, have lost six league games in a row and named Jurgen Streppel coach on 28 October, after Adrie Koster's interim spell ended in a 1-6 home defeat to Cambuur. This is Streppel's second game in charge. PEC Zwolle are under caretaker Dennis van der Ree after Henry van der Vegt left and are unbeaten in four league games, but they went out of the cup at TOP Oss last week.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, largely because Willem II have conceded 25 in their last six. A new coach in a relegation scrap usually fixes the defence first, and Zwolle have scored only 6 in their last six, so we lean a little lower. Both defences are weak, though, so this lean is mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners. Nothing in the news changes how either side attacks. Willem II should push at home under Streppel, and Zwolle's 4-3-3 is expected to be unchanged from last weekend.

cards.text: The numbers say about 3 cards. Desperation at the bottom could raise the temperature, but we found nothing on referee Allard Lindhout's style or on any feud between the clubs to move this number.

shots.text: The numbers say 30 shots. Willem II are expected to name an unchanged 4-4-1-1, and Zwolle field their usual side. We found nothing that changes the expected volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. The absences are fringe players: Hoogma and Lachkar for Willem II, and Floranus, Krastev and Rahajaän for Zwolle. None of them changes the attacking quality much.

401884739.overall: This is a relegation six-pointer before the international break. Hamburg are 15th after two straight league defeats and have only four open-play goals this season. Gladbach are bottom but unbeaten in three, with their first clean sheet in a 0-0 at Paderborn. Gladbach coach Alexander Blessin was reported unwell this week, and his side are missing several attackers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Hamburg's attack has been toothless (only Schalke have fewer open-play goals), and Fabio Vieira is still out. Gladbach are without Nicolas Kühn, Hugo Bolin and Tim Kleindienst. With so much at stake at the bottom, a cagey game looks likelier than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Polzin expects an evenly matched game against a pressing Gladbach side, and nothing in the team news points clearly to more or fewer corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. This is a scrap between 15th and 18th: Blessin wants a 'hungry' team, and Polzin's side could drop into the bottom three with a loss. Gladbach's aggressive pressing also tends to produce fouls, so we lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots. Gladbach have lost their main forward options in Kühn, Bolin and Kleindienst (Kleindienst only returns after the break), and Hamburg have struggled to create in open play. Poulsen, Capaldo and Bornauw were all doubtful.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. With Hamburg's weak finishing and Gladbach missing their best attackers, we expect fewer efforts to test either goalkeeper. Gladbach are also without their first-choice keeper, Moritz Nicolas, which may tempt Hamburg to shoot from range.

401876405.overall: Toulouse (12th, 10 points) and Strasbourg (13th, 10 points) meet in midtable. Toulouse lost 2-0 at Marseille after a five-game unbeaten run. Strasbourg ended four straight defeats by beating Auxerre 5-1. Strasbourg's league games have averaged four goals this season (17 scored, 19 conceded in 9).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Strasbourg's games are high-scoring, and their attack looks restored with Doukouré, Nanasi and Godo back for the Auxerre rout. Toulouse lose winger Aron Dønnum to suspension and on-loan Alexis Amougou (ineligible against his parent club), which slightly blunts them, but the Strasbourg factor points up.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners. Both coaches are expected to use their usual systems, and nothing in the news points either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. This is not a grudge or relegation game, and we found nothing on referee Mathieu Vernice's recent form that would move the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots. Strasbourg have only Baldé and Panichelli missing, and Toulouse's probable XI with Tengstedt and Russell-Rowe up front is close to full strength apart from Dønnum.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Strasbourg's attack is in form after scoring five, and their games tend to be open, so we lean slightly higher.

401874815.overall: The bottom two meet: Venezia are last with 3 points and Udinese 19th with 5. Udinese sacked Kosta Runjaic after a 5-2 home defeat to Roma, and Paolo Zanetti makes his debut at the Penzo. Davide Nicola replaced Giovanni Stroppa at Venezia in October. Zanetti says he will keep the back three for now and wants a team that 'runs, works and presses'.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Venezia have scored only 2 in their last six, and Udinese only 3. A new coach's first game in a relegation six-pointer usually starts with caution and a focus on defence. Udinese's leaky defence (23 conceded in 10) is the main risk to this lean.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Both teams play wing-backs (Venezia 3-5-2, Udinese 3-4-2-1), and nothing in the team news changes the expected flow.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. This is a high-pressure last-v-second-last game, with a new Udinese coach demanding intensity and a small, loud stadium. We expect more fouls and bookings than a normal game. Referee Juan Luca Sacchi's card tendencies were not reported.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.2 shots. Venezia's probable XI with Adams and Yeboah up front is close to full strength. Udinese may be without a fully fit Keinan Davis but have Solet back. Nothing clearly moves the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Both attacks have been among the league's weakest in recent weeks, and Davis's fitness is uncertain. In a cautious six-pointer, we lean slightly lower.

401882809.overall: Sixth-placed Sevilla host a struggling Alavés side under Quique Sánchez Flores. Coach Luis García Plaza spent three years at Alavés. Both camps are affected by the death of former Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel, and García Plaza said the game should not have been played. Sevilla are without Peque (hamstring), which the site's list misses, plus Marcão, Miguel Sierra and the suspended Manu Bueno.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Alavés have scored just 4 in their last six, and Quique's priority is rebuilding defensive solidity and confidence. Sevilla lose Peque's creativity, and Isaac Romero is carrying a knee knock. García Plaza himself admits Sevilla aren't scoring enough when they dominate.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners. García Plaza describes Alavés as a five-at-the-back side with big target forwards and a heavy reliance on crosses, which tends to produce corners. Sevilla also expect to have long spells of possession at home.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already high. García Plaza expects players on both sides to be cautious after this week's tragedy, but Sevilla games have been heated (Bueno's red at Getafe). These roughly cancel out.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.3 shots. Sevilla may pair Robbie Ure with Stassin or Romero, and Alavés have everyone available except long-term absentees Mikel Rodríguez and Facundo Garcés. Nothing clearly moves the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. Losing Peque and doubts over Romero slightly weaken Sevilla's finishing. A home side that has dominated games recently offsets that, so we stay with the number.

401879242.overall: Everton (7th, 13 points) come in after a 1-0 win at Newcastle that ended a two-game league losing run; David Moyes's side have kept four clean sheets and their league games have averaged about two goals. Coventry (16th) have won three of their last five under Frank Lampard, the former Everton boss, but have failed to score in five of nine league games and have scored only twice in four away matches. Coventry are without Amenda, Woolfenden, Eccles and Haji Wright, Bobby Thomas and Onyeka are doubts, and Jack Grealish's return for Everton after a disciplinary absence is unclear.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Everton keep winning by narrow margins (1-0 at Newcastle, 1-0 against Ipswich and Wolves), their league games average about two goals, and they have four clean sheets in nine. Coventry have drawn a blank in five of nine and scored just twice away from home, so a tight, low-scoring night looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Everton should have more of the ball against a Coventry side expected to sit in with Awoniyi as their lone outlet, but the news gives no clear reason to move far from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already raised for Stuart Attwell's record. Lampard's return to his old club adds some edge, but neither side is described as card-prone, and the news gives no reason to move the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots. Everton should take most of them against a Coventry back line missing Amenda and Woolfenden and possibly Bobby Thomas, but Moyes's side often settle for control once ahead, which keeps the total around the model's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. Thierno Barry leads Everton's attack and Awoniyi leads Coventry's, but the news gives no clear reason to move this number either way.

401885399.overall: The table has turned the model's history around: Arouca are 5th with 20 points and have won four in a row since Vítor Severino took over without conceding a league goal, while Famalicão are 11th on 10 points. Famalicão lost 3-0 at Braga last time out, are led by interim coach Ricardo Silva (whose future will be decided after this game), had no rest day before this Friday match and are without the suspended Rodrigo Pinheiro. Arouca are missing Puche and Pedro Santos through injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Arouca have not conceded a league goal in four games under Severino, who says this match needs a careful plan of knowing when to attack space and when to drop off. Famalicão have just been beaten 3-0 by Braga, are without Pinheiro and are playing on short rest, which points to a cagey game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. If Arouca sit deeper as Severino suggested, Famalicão may win more corners at home, but their attacking form has dipped, so the two effects roughly cancel.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already high for this fixture's history and Arouca's recent bookings. With an interim coach playing for his job there is pressure, but nothing in the news clearly pushes the number higher or lower.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.7 shots. Arouca's recent run has been built on defensive control, and a tired Famalicão side playing on short rest after the Braga defeat may struggle to create much volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. Arouca's four straight clean sheets under Severino suggest they limit good chances, and Famalicão are missing Pinheiro, so a slightly lower figure looks reasonable.

401878758.overall: Leeds (12th, 11 points) are winless in five league games, have scored only two goals in that run and have drawn five of nine; Daniel Farke is under some scrutiny. Tottenham under Roberto De Zerbi have won three in a row (Coventry, Chelsea, Crystal Palace), scoring seven and conceding one. Leeds have injury doubts over Noah Okafor (groin, reported out), Anton Stach (foot), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (foot) and Joe Rodon, while Spurs are without Bergvall, Mudryk, Adarabioyo, Odobert and Xavi Simons, with James Maddison and Micky van de Ven reported as fitness concerns.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Leeds have scored just twice in their last five games and could be without Okafor, Stach and possibly Calvert-Lewin, which takes most of their threat away. Spurs have conceded once in three games and are short of attacking players with Simons, Odobert and Mudryk out and Maddison a doubt.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Spurs should have more of the ball, but the injuries on both sides do not clearly change how often each team gets into wide areas.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, already raised for John Brooks's record. Reports differ on whether Rodrigo Bentancur is still suspended or back on the bench, and nothing else in the news points the number either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. A Leeds attack missing Okafor and maybe Stach and Calvert-Lewin has been blunt for weeks, and Spurs are without several creative players, so the total looks a little high.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. With Leeds scoring twice in five games and Spurs short of Simons, Odobert and possibly Maddison, clean chances may be scarce.

401882812.overall: Málaga are bottom with 5 points and still looking for a first league win under Juanfran Funes, so they need to go for this game at La Rosaleda. Racing (José Alberto) lost 0-3 to Real Madrid and have taken no points away from home. Racing are without Álvaro Mantilla (cruciate ligament) and key attacker Andrés Martín (hamstring), and Manu Hernando (illness) and Maguette Gueye (muscle) are doubts. Málaga are missing Ochoa and Lobete, Juan Cruz is doubtful, and Pablo Martínez is managing plantar fasciitis.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Racing's poor away defence and Málaga's need to win point to goals, but losing Andrés Martín takes a big piece out of Racing's attack, so the two effects roughly cancel.

corners.text: The numbers say 13.2 corners, already very high. Málaga chasing a first win at home should push for set pieces, but that is largely priced into the model, and there is no news to move it further.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. A bottom-of-the-table side in a must-win home game can make for a tense match, but no referee has been named yet, and the news gives no clear direction.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.9 shots. Málaga should attack with Adrián Niño, Dani Lorenzo and Larrubia, and Racing remain open away from home, but Racing will be short of Andrés Martín's output. The model's figure looks fair.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both defences have let through plenty of chances, which the model already accounts for, and the team news does not clearly change the picture.

401874791.overall: Frosinone, coached by Massimiliano Alvini, are the surprise of the season: 6th with 20 points after back-to-back wins, including 2-0 against Torino. Cagliari have been stuck on 13 points for four games under Fabio Pisacane, and their attack is thin with Nzola and Fadera out until the Como trip, which leaves Mendy as the main striker. Frosinone are without striker Antonio Raimondo, with Birligea set to lead the line.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already lowered for Raimondo and Nzola being out. Frosinone's attack is in form and Cagliari have leaked goals, but Cagliari's attack is short of options, so the model's middle ground looks right.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners. Frosinone's brave 4-2-3-1 with Ghedjemis and Kvernadze out wide should win corners, which the model already reflects, and the news gives no reason to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already raised a lot for referee Giovanni Ayroldi's record. Cagliari's winless run adds some pressure, but nothing in the news points clearly either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.8 shots, pushed up mainly by Frosinone's last six games. With Cagliari short of forwards (Nzola and Fadera out, so it rests on Mendy) and Frosinone missing Raimondo, that total looks stretched.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Both sides are without a first-choice striker (Nzola for Cagliari, Raimondo for Frosinone), which makes a slightly lower figure more likely.

401874811.overall: Torino (10th under Ignazio Abate) have lost two in a row, 3-1 to Como and 2-0 at Frosinone, after three straight wins. Lecce are in a relegation fight and arrive on three straight defeats (0-2 v Juventus, 5-1 at Frosinone, 1-2 v Genoa), with Pierotti, Berisha, Geubbels, Monteiro and Ilic all reported unavailable. Gaspar returns from a two-match ban for Lecce.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Lecce's defence has been leaking (five at Frosinone), but their attack loses Pierotti, Berisha and Geubbels, and Torino have failed to score in their last game. Those two things roughly cancel out, so we see no reason to move off the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Both sides are expected in their usual shapes (Torino 3-5-2 with wing-backs, Lecce 4-3-3), and none of the team news points clearly to more or fewer corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.1 cards, which looks low for this game. Lecce are in a relegation scrap after three straight defeats, and Torino need a result after two losses, so this could be a tense, scrappy game. Ermanno Feliciani referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots. Torino should have the edge at home with Adams and Simeone up front and Vlasic behind them, while a weakened Lecce attack balances that out. Nothing new points either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. The team news doesn't give a clear reason to move away from the model.

401884737.overall: Promoted Paderborn (14th, 9 points) have drawn 0-0 in each of their last two league games and have won both of their league games this season at home. Frankfurt (8th) beat Hamburg 3-1 last time out, but Mario Götze is out with an ear infection, and captain Robin Koch (knee) is in a race to be fit. Adi Hütter expects a grinding game against an 'unpleasant opponent'.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Paderborn come in on two straight goalless draws and Hütter is expecting a grind. Frankfurt are also without Götze, and Burkardt and Ebnoutalib are sharing the striker role, so we expect a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Nothing in the team news changes how either side is likely to attack wide, so we stay with the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards. A tight, grinding game could add a booking, but there is no specific discipline news. Bastian Dankert referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 30 shots. Paderborn's recent games have been low-event (two 0-0s), and Frankfurt are without Götze, one of their creators. We expect a bit fewer shots than the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Two goalless draws in a row for Paderborn and Götze's absence for Frankfurt point to slightly fewer clear efforts.

401884740.overall: Bayern are unbeaten, joint top on 18 points and won 2-0 at Atlético on Tuesday, but Vincent Kompany is still absent after his collapse and hospital stay, so an assistant leads the team. Bayern are also short of attackers: Díaz, Gnabry, Musiala and Saibari are out. Mainz were beaten 4-1 at Elversberg, have lost four of their last five games in all competitions, have conceded 17 league goals in six, and are without the suspended Stefan Posch.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Mainz's defence is the leakiest in the league over the last six games (17 conceded, six inside the first 15 minutes) and Posch is suspended, which points up. Bayern, though, are without Díaz, Gnabry, Musiala and Saibari, and Olise took a knock against Dortmund, which points down. Overall we stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Bayern should dominate the ball as usual, and nothing in the news shifts the corner picture.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Mainz under pressure at home could get more physical, but there is no specific news on discipline beyond Posch's ban. Robert Schröder referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots. Bayern have the league's highest xG and most big chances, and Kane, with six goals in five league games against Mainz, is expected to start. Their attacking absences stop us going higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 shots on target. Mainz are conceding a lot of chances, but a weakened Bayern front line balances that out.

401884744.overall: Leipzig (5th) host Augsburg (15th, one win in seven) three days after a Champions League game against Manchester City, and Martín Demichelis may rotate. Augsburg are without the suspended Juma Bah, plus Banks, Mounié, Breithaupt and Brackelmann (concussion). Leipzig have scored in eight straight games, while Augsburg have scored in ten straight and conceded in eight straight.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals. Augsburg's defence is weakened with Bah suspended and Brackelmann out, and both sides have long scoring runs. Possible Leipzig rotation after the City game holds us back from going higher than the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Leipzig should dominate territory at home, and nothing in the news changes that.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. Augsburg's defensive changes could lead to some tactical fouls, but there is no specific discipline news. Daniel Schlager referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.3 shots. Leipzig's attack, led by the in-form Nusa, should create plenty, but a rotated XI after the Champions League is a small brake.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target. The news doesn't give a clear reason to move away from the model.

Marcel Sabitzer is back in training after illness. Promoted Elversberg are a surprise 7th on 13 points, beat Mainz 4-1 last week, and bring more than 8,000 fans. Kovac says Dortmund are coming off an intense run of games before the international break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. Dortmund lose their main striker, Guirassy, and have only seven league goals in their last six games anyway. Elversberg have stood up to every opponent so far, according to Kovac, so we expect fewer goals than the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.1 corners. Dortmund should still have most of the ball at home, and without Guirassy that pressure is likely to produce corners rather than clean chances.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. There is no specific discipline news. Harm Osmers referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Dortmund should still pile up attempts at home, though without Guirassy the quality is likely to suffer more than the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Without Guirassy, Dortmund lack their main finisher, and the tiredness after Tuesday's Champions League game could cost some sharpness in front of goal.

401878760.overall: Arsenal top the table with 24 points and are the only side in the league with a 100% home record. They host promoted Hull, who are 11th but have gone eight games without a win in all competitions. Arsenal played Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday and are without Bukayo Saka (quad), Max Dowman (suspended) and possibly Ezri Konsa, who was substituted early in Prague. Hull lose Matt Crooks to a fifth-yellow ban on top of a long injury list.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Arsenal win at home but don't run up big scores: 14 goals in nine league games. With Saka out and legs tired after Prague, Arteta's side may be more about control than goals. Hull under Sergej Jakirovic have a joint-high five league draws and tend to keep games tight.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10 corners, most of them Arsenal's. Hull are likely to defend deep away at the league leaders, and Hull's injury list leaves them few ways to relieve pressure. That points to Arsenal pinning them back and forcing plenty of blocked crosses and set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, with most expected from Hull. Hull lose Matt Crooks, their experienced, tough-tackling midfielder who is suspended after his fifth booking. Oli McBurnie is one booking away from a ban. A one-sided game in which Arsenal keep the ball usually produces fewer flashpoints.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots, roughly 17 of them Arsenal's. Hull sitting deep fits a high Arsenal shot count. Missing Saka and possibly rotating after the Champions League pulls the other way, so the model's figure looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Without Saka, Arsenal lose their main source of chances from the right. A packed Hull defence should block plenty of efforts, and Hull have rarely tested goalkeepers away from home.

401879241.overall: Two struggling sides meet at Craven Cottage. Fulham (15th) are unbeaten in three under Alvaro Arbeloa after starting the season winless in six. Matthias Jaissle's Newcastle (13th) have lost four of their last five, most recently 1-0 at home to Everton. Newcastle are short in midfield: Joelinton is injured, Jacob Ramsey is suspended after a red card against Everton, and Lewis Miley and Matias Fernandez-Pardo are doubts.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Newcastle have scored only six in their last six, and Fulham have conceded just four over the same run. Fulham's striker Gonzalo Garcia has not scored in his last eight league starts. With both teams worried about the relegation zone, a cautious, tight game looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say about 11 corners, split fairly evenly. Nothing in the team news clearly moves this figure. Fulham pressing a weakened Newcastle midfield could add a few home corners, but there is no strong reason to move away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Robert Jones referees a tense game between two sides looking over their shoulders. Newcastle had a man sent off last time out, but they lose Ramsey, one of their combative midfielders, so we stay close to the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Newcastle's attack has stalled, and a reshuffled midfield without Joelinton and Ramsey should create less. Fulham have recently been more solid than dangerous, so the total could come in a little under the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Both teams' recent finishing has been poor: Newcastle are well below their expected goals over six games, and Garcia's drought continues. That points to slightly fewer efforts on target than the model expects.

401882813.overall: Espanyol have just appointed Eder Sarabia after sacking Manolo González, but Sarabia is serving the last game of a touchline ban carried over from Elche, so assistant Jon López leads the team. The 'Eder Sarabia suspended' entry in the site's absence list is this coaching ban, not a player. Espanyol are one point above the drop and without a home win in four. goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Espanyol are without their striker Kike García (hamstring) and have scored only five in their last six. Deportivo have not won away since the fourth matchday. A new coaching staff's first priority is usually to be hard to beat, which points to a cagey game.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10.7 corners, split evenly. Sarabia's focus on pressing and quick ball progression could push Espanyol forward early, but Hidalgo himself says he is 'going in blind' about how Espanyol will set up. No clear reason to move away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, typical of LaLiga. A new-coach lift and a nervous home crowd could add intensity, but Espanyol lose Roger Hinojo, who is suspended for yellow-card accumulation, and the sombre mood may calm things. Nothing points clearly either way.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Sarabia wants a pressing, front-foot side, which could lift Espanyol's volume. Losing Kike García and possibly Jofre Carreras (adductor) works against it, so the two roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9 shots on target. Without Kike García, Espanyol are short of a reliable finisher, and Javi Puado is only just back from injury. Deportivo's away attack has been flat. Expect slightly fewer shots on target than the model.

401875555.overall: Danny Buijs's Fortuna Sittard are sixth and unbeaten in six league games, but they have taken only seven points from 15 at home. Henk Brugge's Telstar are near the bottom. They beat Utrecht 4-2 for their first win since the opening weekend, then went out of the KNVB Beker to Almere City in midweek. Fortuna have doubts over Rodrigo Guth and Lequincio Zeefuik, and Telstar over Gerald Alders.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Fortuna have the lowest possession in the league and play a compact, counter-attacking game. Their recent run includes three draws and a 1-0 home win, which points to tighter games than the model expects. Telstar's away record is poor, with one win in five, although Tyrone Owusu is in form with five goals in five games.

corners.text: The numbers say about 10.7 corners. Fortuna's low-possession style could hand Telstar more of the ball and some corners, but nothing in the news strongly moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards, a low figure for a game with Dennis Higler refereeing. We found no news on discipline or bad blood between the clubs, so we stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say about 28 shots. Fortuna rarely have the ball, averaging 35.7% possession, and rely on making the most of a few clear chances. That usually means fewer total shots from them. Telstar played a cup tie in midweek, which may take some edge off their pressing.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, which is high. Fortuna convert big chances well but don't fire many efforts, and Telstar have struggled to create away from home. A total just under 10 looks more realistic.

401885398.overall: Nacional, low in the table with seven points, have new coach João Henriques. He has made them hard to break down with a back five, and they have not conceded from open play recently, including against Braga and Arouca. Bruno Pinheiro's Académico de Viseu are sixth with 20 points. Pinheiro expects a 'patient' game and says creating chances from open play will be one of the biggest challenges.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Under Henriques, Nacional have prioritised defence, with a back five and only one set-piece goal conceded recently. Pinheiro himself says Nacional have 'closed the doors' to their goal. Nacional have scored only four in their last six, so a low-scoring game looks likely.

corners.text: The numbers say about 8.8 corners. If Viseu have most of the ball against a deep Nacional block, they could win more corners than the model gives them, but Nacional's home share would likely drop. That roughly evens out.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, with Pedro Ramalho refereeing. A patient, low-tempo game against a deep defence doesn't obviously add bookings, and we found no disciplinary news for either side.

shots.text: The numbers say almost 30 shots, which looks high for this game. Nacional's back five is built to limit openings, and Pinheiro expects a slow, patient build-up from his side. That points to fewer shots overall.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Viseu's coach openly expects to struggle to create clear chances against Nacional's new set-up. Nacional's attack has been weak, with four goals in six games. Expect fewer efforts on target than the model.

401874974.overall: An Emilia derby between two sides in good spirits: Parma won 3-0 at Atalanta on Monday in Alberto Gilardino's first game, and Raffaele Palladino's Bologna have won three in a row. Neither side played in Europe this week, and the absentees match the site's list (Bernabé and Drobnic for Parma; Holm, De Silvestri and Enem for Bologna).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Parma are expected in a 3-5-2 that defends deep, which fits a low total, but both sides arrive scoring freely, so nothing pushes us either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Nothing in the team news changes how either side builds attacks, so we stay with the numbers.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. It's a local derby between two teams with momentum, and Palladino expects a physical Parma that presses high at times, so we lean a little higher. We found no recent record for referee Luca Zufferli, so this rests on the occasion alone.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.6 shots. Bologna's front three (Bernardeschi, Odgaard, Cambiaghi) should see most of the ball, as the numbers already expect, and we found nothing to move it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.1 shots on target. No news points either way.

401884743.overall: Stuttgart lost a heated 2-0 game at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday, though they created plenty (Leweling hit the post twice), and Hoeneß says some rotation is possible. Bremen are 5th, unbeaten in seven and six points ahead of Stuttgart, with Füllkrug the league's top scorer. Bremen are missing eight senior players, but Niklas Stark (listed as out on the site) is not on their absentee list and may return. Karazor is a doubt after a knock in Istanbul.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Bremen arrive with a depleted squad but in form behind Füllkrug, and Stuttgart's midfield is thin without Stiller and possibly Karazor, which tends to open games up. We lean slightly higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners. Stuttgart should have most of the ball at home, which the numbers already reflect, so we stay level.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already a high figure. We found nothing on referee Sören Storks or on bad blood between the clubs that would push it further.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.9 shots. Stuttgart created a lot even in defeat in Istanbul and won 4-2 at Leverkusen last time out in the league, and Bremen like to counter through Füllkrug, so we lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target. Possible rotation after the midweek game cuts against the higher shot count, so we stay level.

401882811.overall: Osasuna, back under Jagoba Arrasate, are 15th and rely heavily on Budimir (8 goals). Aimar Oroz and Jorge Herrando are out rather than doubtful, as several reports confirm. Edin Terzić's Athletic have won three league games in a row but have only Iñaki Williams as a fit senior striker, since Guruzeta and Sannadi are injured. Nico Williams and Yuri are back in training.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Both coaches expect a tight game, Terzić pointing out that Osasuna's games have had few goals. Osasuna lose Oroz, their main creator, and Athletic have no striker depth, so we lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Athletic's direct, transition style and Arrasate's plan to go long at times balance out, so we stay with the numbers.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Terzić expects a game of many duels in a 'hot' El Sadar, and Athletic will hold a very high line, which tends to bring tactical fouls on the break. We lean slightly higher, though we found no recent record for referee Sesma Espinosa.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots. Nothing in the news moves the volume either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. With Oroz out for Osasuna and Athletic's forward line thin, we lean a little lower on quality chances.

401878757.overall: Forest are 19th under Oliver Glasner and have not scored in any of their four home league games, despite taking the second most shots in the league. City won 3-2 at RB Leipzig in midweek after losing their last two league games (at Villa, home to Brighton), and Dias and Gvardiol may return. Reports disagree on whether Forest's Igor Jesus is back from a calf injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Forest have failed to score in every home league game this season and convert about 4% of their shots, so the home side's share looks generous. City's chances keep us from leaning far, so this lean is mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Forest shoot often from range, and City should dominate the ball, two habits that tend to produce blocked shots and corners. We lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. One profile describes Samuel Barrott as a low-key referee who lets play flow, so we lean slightly lower. That comes from a single source.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots. Forest have the second-highest shot count in the league even while losing, and City carry the league's best xG, so we lean higher on volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Forest's high volume comes with poor accuracy, which offsets the higher shot count, so we stay level.

401875552.overall: ADO Den Haag sacked coach Robin Peter this week, and assistant Levi Schwiebbe takes charge for this one. Maurice Steijn is reported as the likely successor but was not confirmed as of Friday. ADO are 17th and have lost three in a row. Sparta, near the drop zone, won 3-2 at Groningen and are expected to set up with a back five. Toornstra went off early at Groningen and one report lists him only as a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Sparta's expected back five and the caution of a relegation six-pointer, with a stand-in coach on ADO's bench, point to a tighter game than the attacking ratings suggest. We lean slightly lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Nothing in the news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. It's a South Holland derby with relegation at stake and a caretaker coach for ADO, so we lean higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots. ADO at home should push, but Sparta's back five will limit space, so we stay with the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. A packed Sparta defence and two struggling attacks suggest fewer clean chances, so we lean a little lower.

401876411.overall: Liam Rosenior's Paris FC are 4th after a 3-1 win over Monaco, in which they outshot them 19 to 9 with a high press. Will Still's Auxerre are 14th, lost 5-1 at Strasbourg and have conceded in five straight games, though they are unbeaten in three at home. Dioubaté is suspended after his red card there. L'Équipe reports Labeau-Lascary is back, while Tuanzebe is a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. Auxerre's defence has leaked in every recent game and Paris FC arrive attacking with confidence, so we lean higher. Both previous league meetings were draws, the last 0-0, which keeps the lean mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Nothing in the news changes either side's approach to wide play.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already above average. Auxerre's red card last week hints at frustration, but we found nothing on referee Marc Bollengier, so we stay level.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. Paris FC took 19 shots against Monaco with a high press, and Auxerre have been giving up chances, so we lean higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. Paris FC put 10 on target against Monaco, and Auxerre's defence is short of bodies without Okoh and possibly Tuanzebe, so we lean higher.

401885402.overall: Alverca (10th) have lost three in a row without scoring, including a cup exit at Tondela. Casa Pia are 17th with the joint-lowest goal tally in the league (5), and all seven of their points came away from home. Alverca coach Sérgio Ferreira wants a compact low block, and Casa Pia's Filipe Coelho admits finishing is their main problem. Alverca keeper Jhonatan Luiz is a doubt.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Alverca have not scored in three games, Casa Pia have scored only five all season, and Alverca plan to sit in a compact block. We lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. Nothing in the news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. We found nothing on referee Sérgio Guelho or any special tension, so we stay level.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. A home side defending in a low block and an away side short of attacking quality point to a cagey game, so we lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Both attacks are misfiring, so we lean lower.

401874803.overall: Roma are unbeaten in Serie A with the league's best attack, but they lost 3-2 at Manchester United on Tuesday after leading 2-0, and one report says only 16 outfield players are available. Svilar is out, Gollini is a late call with a back problem, and Dybala and Manu Koné are unlikely to feature. Sassuolo have lost four league games in a row and have the worst defence, and they are without Domenico Berardi, who is missing from the site's list.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. Roma come in tired and short of bodies, and Sassuolo lose their main creator Berardi, which the numbers don't count. Sassuolo's leaky defence keeps this lean mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Roma should dominate territory as the numbers expect, and we found nothing to change that.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards. We found nothing on referee Marco Di Bello or any tension between the sides, so we stay level.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots. Roma's depleted squad pulls one way and Sassuolo's poor defending the other, so we stay with the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. Without Dybala and with Sassuolo's attack weakened by Berardi's absence, we lean slightly lower on chances worked into shots on target.

401875554.overall: Excelsior lost 0-9 at home to Twente last weekend after Nesto Groen was sent off early, and coach Den Uil called it a mental collapse. They have one point from their last six games. Go Ahead Eagles lost 4-0 at Cambuur in a game abandoned late for fireworks, with the result standing. Their games this season have been open, and Tengstedt has eight goals.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already high. Excelsior's defence has collapsed recently, but their attack has failed to score in three of four, so the two pull against each other and we stay with the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Nothing in the news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards. We found nothing on referee Jeroen Manschot, and the crowd tension after the Cambuur incident has been handled with travel restrictions for away fans, so we stay level.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. No news points either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. Go Ahead create a lot through Tengstedt and Edvardsen, and Excelsior's defence has been easy to get through, so we lean slightly higher.

401882808.overall: Javier Aguirre's Valencia are in the relegation zone and have not won at home in the league this season. José Mourinho's Real Madrid have won seven league games in a row, but this is their third away game in seven days after a 3-2 comeback win at AEK on Wednesday. Vinícius serves the last game of his ban, and Mendy is left out of the squad. Valencia are expected to sit in a back five and counter.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Without Vinícius, after a tiring trip to Athens and against a Valencia side set to defend with five, we lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Madrid should have long spells on the ball against a deep block, as the numbers already expect, so we stay level.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. A relegation-threatened Valencia in a hostile Mestalla against Madrid usually makes for a combative game, so we lean higher. We found no recent record for referee Hernández Maeso.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. Madrid will have the ball, but Valencia's low block and Madrid's fatigue cancel out, so we stay with the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. With Vinícius out and Valencia defending deep, more of Madrid's shots should come from distance or be blocked, so we lean slightly lower.

401876407.overall: PSG lead Ligue 1, have won six league games in a row and beat Villarreal 6-0 in midweek, but they are without Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes and Akliouche. Hakimi is also rested until the international break, which the site does not count. Troyes are 16th and have failed to score in five of nine games, but they have kept two clean sheets in a row, and their coach says they won't park the bus.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Without Hakimi as well as Dembélé and Kvaratskhelia, PSG's attack is short of key players, and Troyes have kept two clean sheets in a row, so we lean slightly lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners. PSG will have long spells of possession against a side sitting in its own half, which tends to produce corners, so we lean higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards. We could not confirm the referee or find anything pointing to a heated game, so we stay level.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots. PSG's dominance should hold even with rotation, as the numbers expect.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. With so many first-choice attackers out, we expect fewer clean chances than PSG's recent run suggests, so we lean slightly lower.

401885395.overall: Paulo Fonseca takes charge of Sporting for the first time after Rui Borges was sacked on 1 November. Sporting won 1-0 against Shakhtar in midweek under an interim coach. Fonseca says he wants to defend better and press man-to-man. Reports name João Gonçalves as referee, not João Ferreira as the site lists. Moreirense are 9th, have won their last two, and Domingues and Mendonça are doubts.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. A new coach often gives a lift, but Fonseca's first priority is defending better, and Moreirense arrive in form, so the two balance out.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Fonseca says Sporting will play positional attack about 80% of the time, and a pressing, possession side at home against a team that will sit tends to win corners, so we lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, but they assume a different referee: reports name João Gonçalves, not João Ferreira. Sporting's Maxi Araújo and Luis Suárez are one yellow from a ban before a big run of games, which may make them careful. We lean slightly lower.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots. Nothing points either way beyond the uncertainty of a new coach.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. No news points either way.
